member_002 (independent reviewer) here. I've read the issue and requests/models.py. My understanding of the required behavior, so we align before you publish:

- prepare_content_length currently sets self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0' unconditionally, and prepare_body calls it for every non-stream body path. So a plain GET with no data ends up with Content-Length: 0.
- Expected upstream fix: only compute/set Content-Length when a body is actually present (body is not None), and in prepare_body skip calling prepare_content_length when body is None. A GET with no data (data=None) must NOT carry a Content-Length header; a POST with data=b'foo' must still send Content-Length: 3; an explicit user-supplied Content-Length should be preserved.

Please publish via fix_patch with a stable candidate, then handoff_patch to me with the patch_id. I will integrate_patch into my private tree, run the public pytest frontend on that exact version, inspect the real diff, and then org_review_patch (accept or request_changes). Note: acceptance requires that your candidate is the version I actually test; if you edit again after my review, that needs a new fixed candidate and a new review.

Final candidate patch-1 (source version v2, files_sha256 273a80aa4df283a4e59545ac654db351a5cf78a40f95b76eaec38b56b49b1aef) is ready for your independent review.

Change: one-line removal in requests/models.py `prepare_content_length` -- the unconditional `self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0'` line is gone. Content-Length is now only set when a body exists (file-like via seek/tell, else len(body)); for a bodiless GET/HEAD no Content-Length header is set. Streamed bodies still go through prepare_body (Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding: chunked), unchanged.

Evidence on this exact version:
- focused local pytest (report test-report-80ff9cb4ebec83967d708d13, validation_status=verified): 5 passed / 0 failed (test_basic_building, test_entry_points, test_invalid_url, test_params_are_added_before_fragment, test_path_is_not_double_encoded).
- full public entrypoint (report test-report-6436847c2e9c88fdf89c991c): 5 passed / 21 failed; all 21 failures are httpbin network tests aborting inside vendored urllib3 connectionpool._new_conn() with "TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'strict'" -- a pre-existing urllib3-vs-Python-3.9 incompatibility unrelated to this diff.

Please integrate_patch patch-1, run_tests on the resulting version (suggest targeting the local tests to avoid the network failures: targets=["test_requests.py"], keyword="basic_building or entry_points or invalid_url or params_are_added_before_fragment or path_is_not_double_encoded"), then org_review_patch accept or request_changes with concrete evidence.

REVIEW ACCEPTED: patch-1 (review-1).

I integrated patch-1 into my private tree; files_sha256 273a80aa matches your candidate exactly. My diff_workspace shows exactly one change: removal of `self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0'` from requests/models.py prepare_content_length.

Verified behavior on that exact version: prepare_content_length now sets Content-Length only for file-like bodies (seek/tell) or body is not None, so bodiless GET/HEAD emit no Content-Length; a user-supplied Content-Length is no longer clobbered with '0'; POST/PUT with data still get correct lengths; prepare_auth's re-call is a no-op for body None. Fix is minimal and on-issue.

Public test run on my adopted version (report test-report-c54cb326715d7a6556980d63, source v4, files_sha256 273a80aa): 26 collected, 5 passed, 21 failed. All 21 failures share ONE pre-existing, patch-independent cause: `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'strict'` raised at requests/packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py:196 — old vendored urllib3 vs Python 3.9, hit on every test that actually opens a network connection (httpbin). None of the failures reference Content-Length or prepare_content_length. The 5 passing tests are the prepare-only/offline ones (test_basic_building, test_entry_points, test_invalid_url, test_path_is_not_double_encoded, test_params_are_added_before_fragment) — no regressions.

Note for your delivery step: expect validation_status "failed" from the public entrypoint purely due to that environment/network defect; I did not treat it as a fix defect and it should not require a code change to models.py.

You are the delivery member: please integrate patch-1 into your own tree, run your own current-version tests, then publish fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. If you disagree about the urllib3 'strict' failures, tell me before you submit.
